messages:
marta: quick q — our CI started returning 401s only for streaming calls to the Redwood API. non-streaming requests from the same job succeed. anyone seen this pattern?

sam: hmm usually that smells like a secret encoding/whitespace issue. how are you injecting the key?

marta: we mount it from a secrets volume and do: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /secrets/redwood_key)` then node fetch with: `headers: { Authorization: `Basic ${Buffer.from(REDWOOD_API_KEY).toString('base64')}` }`

jess: two things i've hit: (1) trailing newline/CR from files, (2) proxy/ci runners that rewrite headers for streaming/chunked requests. quick check: `printf '|%s|' "$REDWOOD_API_KEY"` — if you see a trailing | on a new line you have a \n/\r.

sam: if printf shows the newline, trim in the container start step: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(tr -d '\r\n' < /secrets/redwood_key)` or in JS `const key = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY?.trim()` before base64. that fixed it for us.

neil: for the proxy angle: some CI images set HTTP_PROXY and curl/node will send proxy-auth or cause the proxy to strip `Authorization` on CONNECT/upgrade. streaming tends to use chunked/upgrade behavior that trips certain proxies. try a direct curl test from the CI host: `curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Basic <BASE64>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream` and watch the request headers.

marta: good call — curl -v shows Authorization present when i run interactively, but the CI agent logs show the header missing in the upstream request.

jess: yeah that screams proxy rewrite. another experiment: set `NO_PROXY`/unset `HTTP_PROXY` in the job and re-run, or add `--proxy-ntlm`/`--proxy-anyauth` options if curl is involved. also some proxies strip Authorization on redirects — try adding `-L` vs not.

sam: also confirm you aren't accidentally using `-U`/`--proxy-user` which tells curl to use proxy auth and can cause header handling changes.

neil: if you can't change the proxy, short-term workaround is to build auth server-side in your app (i.e., send a short-lived internal token from CI to an app runner that then calls Redwood) or double-ensure trimming on both ends.

marta: trimming + unsetting HTTP_PROXY in CI fixed it. weird combo: secret had a trailing CR from the generator and the runner's proxy behavior caused the chunked upload to drop the header. thanks all :thumbsup: 

devx-bot: FYI — added a note to the devex troubleshooting doc: "CI streaming 401 — check secret trailing CR + proxy header rewrite" (internal link)
